path: Four data components that add a chart form the catalog lacks: a box plot, a slope chart, a lollipop chart, and a streamgraph. Every one follows a published method named in its credits, or is a plain arrangement of position along a common scale, and nothing is built from a capture or from anyone's component. Each is one core with an SVG look and a glyph look, a hidden data table, and one accent mark. Nothing fetches from the network, nothing adds a dependency, every default is a pure function of its props, and every default already looks finished on the dark ground and the light one.

components.title: Box Plot
components.brief: The distribution of several groups side by side on one value axis. Each group is a hollow box from its first to its third quartile with a heavy tick across it at the median, a hairline whisker out to each end, and a small mark for every outlier. It follows the box-and-whisker plot as Chambers, Cleveland, Kleiner and Tukey describe it, and it fixes the statistics so the drawing is exact. Input is raw numbers per group. Sort a group's finite values ascending and take a quantile at probability p by linear interpolation between order statistics at position (n - 1) * p, which gives the quartiles and the median. The box runs from Q1 to Q3, and the whiskers reach the most extreme values that lie within 1.5 times the interquartile range of the box. Any value beyond a whisker is an outlier, drawn as a small hollow circle in the SVG look and as a dot glyph in the glyph look. A group with fewer than one finite value draws its label and nothing else, and a group with one value draws a single tick. It is not the bar chart: that draws one total per category as a filled bar from zero, while this draws the spread of many values per category and never fills a box and never needs a zero baseline, so the value axis spans the data with nice ticks from lib/chart.ts. Boxes and whiskers are fg at one weight, the median tick is thicker than the box edge, and the accent marks only the group named by `highlight`, whose median tick is drawn in the accent and whose median value is printed as a direct label beside it, so color never carries meaning alone. Group names sit under their boxes in muted mono. The SVG look draws hairline axes, gridlines, boxes, whiskers with short end caps, and outliers with lib/chart.ts and lib/chart-marks.ts. The glyph look draws the same plot on a cell grid: the box as box-drawing characters, the median as a heavy horizontal glyph, whiskers as vertical box-drawing lines, outliers as a dot glyph, and each row position resolved to a half cell by braille dots from lib/braille-plot.ts where a cell would round a quartile to the wrong row. Follow registry/data/bar-chart for structure, the two looks, the mount, update, and destroy lifecycle, and the hidden table. The hidden table has one row per group with the columns Group, n, Min, Q1, Median, Q3, Max, and Outliers, with the outliers joined into one cell, so assistive technology hears the same five numbers the drawing shows. A capture at 1280 px shows five groups side by side with boxes about a third of the band wide, whiskers, two outliers on different groups, the highlighted group's median in the accent with its label, a value axis at round numbers with hairline gridlines, and an inset of about one em on every side. A capture at 390 px shows the same five groups with narrower boxes, the group names thinned or shortened rather than overlapping, and the axis labels still readable. It is wrong if a box is filled, because the catalog already has filled bars; if the quartiles are computed by index rounding or by splitting the sample in two so that they differ between the two looks; if an outlier is drawn as part of a whisker; if the value axis is forced to start at zero and crushes the boxes into one band; or if two group names overlap at 390 px. Chart rules, restated because a builder starts with nothing: two looks, an SVG one and a glyph one, chosen by `look`; a `label` that names the chart, with the host as role figure named by it, the drawing aria-hidden, and dataTable from lib/chart.ts carrying the numbers in a hidden table; hairline axes and gridlines in muted through lib/chart-marks.ts; tick labels in mono with tabular figures at round values; at most one accent series or mark; direct labels instead of a legend; an inset of about one em so nothing runs to the frame's edge; a redraw on resize; and something sensible when the data is empty, which is the axes and a muted note. Lifecycle and accessibility, identical in both looks: labelHost on the host as a figure, unlabelHost on destroy, the table removed on destroy, data-pica-ready set after the first complete draw and deleted on destroy, a watchPalette redraw when the palette changes, the canvas tint read through readPalette because a canvas cannot resolve a var() reference, and a ResizeObserver that is disconnected on destroy. Text is never in the accent, because mint measures 1.96:1 on paper. Declare the facets static and chart, and let meta.palette list fg, accent, and muted. Data components have 8192 bytes, shared runtime included, and this one is expected near 6.4 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, which here means it takes none at all, and looks finished and intentional on both grounds.
components.props: data (json, [{ label, values }] where values is an array of numbers, default five groups of 15 to 25 fixed values each, such as Build, Test, Lint, Deploy, and Rollback durations in seconds, with each group's spread different and two groups carrying one outlier), label (default "Task duration by stage, in seconds"), highlight (-1 to 20, default -1, which highlights the group with the highest median), whisker (0.5 to 3, default 1.5, the interquartile range multiple that bounds the whiskers), ticks (2 to 10, default 5), look ("svg" or "glyph", default "svg"), fontFamily (GRID_FONT). The inspector exposes every prop except fontFamily.

credits.title: Graphical Methods for Data Analysis
credits.author: John M. Chambers, William S. Cleveland, Beat Kleiner and Paul A. Tukey

components.title: Slope Chart
components.brief: A before and after comparison drawn as two vertical axes with one straight line per item between them. The left axis is the first period and the right axis is the second, both on one shared value scale, so a line's slope is its change and the lines that rise, fall, or cross are the story. It rests on Cleveland and McGill's ranking of graphical perception, which puts position along a common scale first: each end of a line is a position on the same scale, and no angle or area carries a value. The labels do the legend's work. At the left end of each line sits the item's name and its first value, right-aligned against the left axis, and at the right end sits its second value and, when there is room, the name again, left-aligned against the right axis, so nothing needs a key. Labels that would collide are separated by a deterministic relaxation: sort the labels on one side by value with the input index breaking ties, then push neighbours apart to a minimum of one line of text and pull the whole stack back inside the plot, so the same input always yields the same positions, and a short leader hairline joins a nudged label to its true line end. Lines are fg at one weight. The accent marks exactly one line, the one named by `highlight`, drawn heavier with both its values printed, so a viewer finds the item the chart is about, and its label also carries its change as a signed figure, so the accent never carries meaning alone. It is not the line chart: that plots a series over many labels along one axis, while this compares two points per item, so there is no x scale and no gridlines, only the two axes and the value ticks printed once on the far left in muted. It is not the bar chart either: no rectangle is drawn. The SVG look draws the two axes as hairlines, the lines as straight paths through lib/chart.ts, a small filled dot at each end, and labels with lib/chart-marks.ts. The glyph look draws the lines as braille dots through lib/braille-plot.ts between two columns of text labels on a cell grid, with the end dots as a bullet glyph. Follow registry/data/line-chart for the two looks and its lifecycle, since its glyph look resamples through braille the same way. The hidden table has one row per item with the columns Item, the first period's name, the second period's name, and Change. A capture at 1280 px shows eight lines between two axes about 60 percent of the frame apart, at least two lines crossing, one rising line in the accent with a signed change, the column headers naming the two periods above the axes, and every label legible and apart. A capture at 390 px keeps both axes, shortens the plot to what the labels leave, drops the repeated name at the right end first, and still shows every line and every value without overlap. It is wrong if two labels overlap at either width; if a line is a curve, because a slope must be a straight segment between its two true positions; if the two axes use different scales; if a label is placed by input order rather than by value so that its line and its label drift apart without a leader; or if a legend, a gridline, or a filled area appears. Chart rules, restated because a builder starts with nothing: two looks, an SVG one and a glyph one, chosen by `look`; a `label` that names the chart, with the host as role figure named by it, the drawing aria-hidden, and dataTable from lib/chart.ts carrying the numbers in a hidden table; hairline axes in muted through lib/chart-marks.ts; tick labels in mono with tabular figures at round values; at most one accent series or mark; direct labels instead of a legend; an inset of about one em so nothing runs to the frame's edge; a redraw on resize; and something sensible when the data is empty, which is the axes and a muted note. Lifecycle and accessibility, identical in both looks: labelHost on the host as a figure, unlabelHost on destroy, the table removed on destroy, data-pica-ready set after the first complete draw and deleted on destroy, a watchPalette redraw when the palette changes, the canvas tint read through readPalette because a canvas cannot resolve a var() reference, and a ResizeObserver that is disconnected on destroy. An item whose value is not a finite number is listed in the table with a blank cell and drawn as a label with no line. Text is never in the accent, because mint measures 1.96:1 on paper. Declare the facets static and chart, and let meta.palette list fg, accent, and muted. Data components have 8192 bytes, shared runtime included, and this one is expected near 6.0 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, which here means it takes none at all, and looks finished and intentional on both grounds.
components.props: data (json, { from, to, rows } where from and to name the two periods and rows is [{ name, a, b }], default from "2023" and to "2025" with eight rows of framework and tool names whose values are percentage shares, such as rows that rise, fall, and cross), label (default "Share of projects by tool, 2023 and 2025"), highlight (-1 to 20, default -1, which highlights the row with the largest absolute change), values (default true, prints both end values), ticks (2 to 10, default 5), look ("svg" or "glyph", default "svg"), fontFamily (GRID_FONT). The inspector exposes every prop except fontFamily.

components.title: Lollipop Chart
components.brief: Ranked values as horizontal rows, each a hairline stem from the baseline to a dot at its value, with the row's name at the left and its figure beside the dot. It rests on Cleveland and McGill's ranking of graphical perception: position along a common scale is read more accurately than length or area, so the dot's position carries the value and the stem is only a guide to the eye, and the thin stem leaves far less ink than a filled bar of the same value. It is not the bar chart: that draws vertical filled bars in input order, while this draws horizontal rows, ranked by default, with a stem and a dot and no filled area, so the two read as different charts and a long list of names fits without rotating a label. Rows are sorted by `sort`: "value" ranks from largest to smallest with the input index breaking ties, and "input" keeps the given order. The baseline is zero, so a negative value draws its stem leftward from the baseline to a dot left of it, and the value axis spans the data and zero with nice ticks from lib/chart.ts, printed once beneath the last row in muted mono with hairline gridlines behind the rows. Stems are fg hairlines, dots are solid fg, and the accent marks only the row named by `highlight`, whose dot is larger and drawn in the accent while its name stays fg, and every figure is printed beside its dot in mono, so the accent never carries meaning alone. The SVG look draws the gridlines and baseline with lib/chart-marks.ts, each stem as a one pixel line, each dot as a circle of about 4 px radius, and the row names right-aligned in a left margin sized from the longest name, truncated with an ellipsis at a limit so the plot always keeps at least half the width. The glyph look draws one text row per item: the name, then a run of box-drawing horizontal glyphs for the stem, then a bullet glyph at the value, with the value resolved to the nearest cell and the figure after it, so the same ranking reads in text. Follow registry/data/bar-chart for structure, the two looks, and the mount, update, and destroy lifecycle. The hidden table has one row per item in the drawn order with the columns Label and Value. A capture at 1280 px shows ten ranked rows with names on the left, thin stems, dots stepping down in value from top to bottom, one accent dot with a larger size, a value axis beneath at round numbers, and an inset of about one em. A capture at 390 px shows the same ten rows with the name column narrower and truncated where needed, the dots and figures still apart, and no horizontal scroll. It is wrong if a stem is thick enough to read as a bar; if the dot's center is not exactly the value's position on the axis, so that a stem and a dot disagree; if the rows are not in the ranked order by default; if a long name pushes the plot narrower than half the frame at 390 px; or if a figure collides with the dot or with the frame's edge on the largest row. Chart rules, restated because a builder starts with nothing: two looks, an SVG one and a glyph one, chosen by `look`; a `label` that names the chart, with the host as role figure named by it, the drawing aria-hidden, and dataTable from lib/chart.ts carrying the numbers in a hidden table; hairline axes and gridlines in muted through lib/chart-marks.ts; tick labels in mono with tabular figures at round values; at most one accent series or mark; direct labels instead of a legend; an inset of about one em so nothing runs to the frame's edge; a redraw on resize; and something sensible when the data is empty, which is the axes and a muted note. Lifecycle and accessibility, identical in both looks: labelHost on the host as a figure, unlabelHost on destroy, the table removed on destroy, data-pica-ready set after the first complete draw and deleted on destroy, a watchPalette redraw when the palette changes, the canvas tint read through readPalette because a canvas cannot resolve a var() reference, and a ResizeObserver that is disconnected on destroy. Text is never in the accent, because mint measures 1.96:1 on paper. Declare the facets static and chart, and let meta.palette list fg, accent, and muted. Data components have 8192 bytes, shared runtime included, and this one is expected near 5.2 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, which here means it takes none at all, and looks finished and intentional on both grounds.
components.props: data (json, [{ label, value }], default ten rows of the catalog's categories with counts, such as Data 12, UI 38, Patterns 12, Motion 10, Shaders 14, ASCII 20, and four more, none negative), label (default "Components by category"), sort ("value" or "input", default "value"), highlight (-1 to 30, default -1, which highlights the largest value), values (default true), ticks (2 to 10, default 5), look ("svg" or "glyph", default "svg"), fontFamily (GRID_FONT). The inspector exposes every prop except fontFamily.

components.title: Streamgraph
components.brief: A stacked area chart whose stack floats around a centre line instead of resting on zero, so each layer is a band whose thickness is its value and the whole is a flowing silhouette. It follows Byron and Wattenberg's study of stacked graphs, from which it takes the vocabulary: a baseline function g0 under the stack, layers ordered by a rule, and thickness as the only carrier of value. The geometry is exact and has no decoration. At sample i, layer k has value v[k][i], and its band runs from the running sum below it to that sum plus its value, with the first band starting at the baseline. The baseline is the symmetric silhouette: g0[i] = minus half the total of every layer at i, so the stack is centered on the middle and the total thickness at every sample equals the sum of the values. Each band's thickness at every sample must therefore equal its value at that sample, and a test of this is the first thing a capture reviewer applies. Negative and non-finite values are clamped to zero before stacking and listed unclamped in the hidden table. Between samples the edges are straight segments, not smoothed curves, so no overshoot can make a band thicker or thinner than its values between samples. Layer order is deterministic and is chosen by `order`: "input" keeps the given order from bottom to top, and "inside-out" follows Byron and Wattenberg's inside-out ordering, which sorts layers by the sample index of their peak value, earliest first, with the input index breaking ties, and then places them one at a time on whichever side of the growing stack is currently thinner, the first layer going to the center and a tie going upward, so the earliest layers sit nearest the center and the latest outward. The same input always yields the same order and the same shape. There is no seeded noise, no wobble, and no decorative wave: the silhouette's shape comes from the data alone, and a flat dataset draws a flat, even band. Tones: the accent marks only the layer named by `highlight`, which also carries its name as a direct label and its value range in the table, and the other layers alternate between fg at full strength and fg at a lower opacity, so neighbours stay distinguishable, with a one pixel hairline in the ground color between bands. Every layer is labeled directly, its name set inside the band at the sample where it is thickest, in the ink color that reads on that fill, or at the right end beside the band when it is too thin, never in a legend. The SVG look draws the time axis along the bottom at round tick labels from lib/chart.ts, and no value axis, because a floating stack has no zero line: instead, one scale bar at the left, a short vertical hairline spanning a round value from niceTicks, labeled with that value in mono, so a viewer can read the thickness. The glyph look draws the same stack on a cell grid with braille dots through lib/braille-plot.ts, each column resampled linearly between samples, each layer filled between its edges, layers told apart by the dot density: solid, and every second dot, alternately, with a blank row of dots between bands; the scale bar is drawn in box-drawing characters. Follow registry/data/line-chart for the two looks, the area path through areaPath, and the lifecycle. The hidden table has one row per sample and one column per layer in the drawn order, with the first column the sample label, so the numbers are all there. A capture at 1280 px shows six layers across twelve samples, with a clear swell in the middle, the highlighted layer in the accent with its name, every other layer named in or beside its band, a time axis, and the scale bar, and the stack's vertical center holds near the middle of the frame. A capture at 390 px shows the same six layers with the labels that do not fit moved to the right end and the axis labels thinned, and no band narrower than one pixel disappearing into a hairline. It is wrong if a band's thickness at any sample differs from its value there, including from rounding a stack to whole pixels one band at a time so that the total drifts; if the layer order changes between renders of the same data; if there is a repeating wave, a smoothing curve, or noise that is not in the data; if the baseline is zero, because that is the stacked area chart; or if a legend appears. Chart rules, restated because a builder starts with nothing: two looks, an SVG one and a glyph one, chosen by `look`; a `label` that names the chart, with the host as role figure named by it, the drawing aria-hidden, and dataTable from lib/chart.ts carrying the numbers in a hidden table; hairline axes in muted through lib/chart-marks.ts; tick labels in mono with tabular figures at round values; at most one accent series or mark; direct labels instead of a legend; an inset of about one em so nothing runs to the frame's edge; a redraw on resize; and something sensible when the data is empty, which is the axes and a muted note. Lifecycle and accessibility, identical in both looks: labelHost on the host as a figure, unlabelHost on destroy, the table removed on destroy, data-pica-ready set after the first complete draw and deleted on destroy, a watchPalette redraw when the palette changes, the canvas tint read through readPalette because a canvas cannot resolve a var() reference, and a ResizeObserver that is disconnected on destroy. Text is never in the accent, because mint measures 1.96:1 on paper. Declare the facets static and chart, and let meta.palette list fg, accent, bg, and muted. Data components have 8192 bytes, shared runtime included, and this one is expected near 6.6 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, which here means it takes none at all, and looks finished and intentional on both grounds.
components.props: data (json, { labels, series } where labels is an array of sample names and series is [{ name, values }] with one value per label, the same shape as line-chart, default twelve monthly labels and six series of builds by team, with fixed non-negative values that swell in the middle months), label (default "Builds per month by team"), order ("inside-out" or "input", default "inside-out"), highlight (-1 to 20, default -1, which highlights the series with the largest total), ticks (2 to 10, default 5, for the time axis and the scale bar's round value), look ("svg" or "glyph", default "svg"), fontFamily (GRID_FONT). The inspector exposes every prop except fontFamily.
